subject: AcmeTech surge: post-incident readout, corrective plan and exec ask
messages:
From: Sally Chen <sally.chen@acmetech.com>

Cc: ops@acmetech.com
Date: 2027-04-03T09:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: sudden spike + 5xxs and latency on Apr 2

Hi Neha,

We saw a large surge of 500/timeout errors and tail latency spikes on Apr 2 between 22:10-22:45 UTC that impacted a portion of our checkout flow (approx 12% of requests failed). Attached are our client-side traces and a small sample of request IDs. The issue resolved when we rolled back the recent batching change on our side, but the pattern suggests requests hit higher queueing and then 5xxs from your side.

Impact: increased checkout failures and user-visible errors; single-week revenue risk for us.

Can we get an RCA, corrective actions and an ETA for permanent fix? We also need an exec readout — our VP of Engineering (Jordan Li) will join.

Sally
Sally Chen
Head of Engineering, AcmeTech

3) Exec readout with our leadership and your VP (Jordan) — proposed Apr 5 14:00 UTC.

— Neha

From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
To: neha.kapoor@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, marcus_lin@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Cc: Sally Chen <sally.chen@acmetech.com>
Date: 2027-04-04T08:30:00-07:00
Subject: RE: sudden spike + 5xxs and latency on Apr 2 — quick technical summary

Folks — quick technical notes from the triage so you have context for the RCA: 
- Symptom: sustained request queue growth on a subset of shards leading to downstream timeouts and elevated 5xxs (502/504).
- Root proximate cause: an unexpected interaction between a new continuous-batching heuristic and prefix KV cache invalidation during a per-tenant rollout. The batching heuristic grouped some variable-length sequences causing long-running GPU kernels; when those kernels stalled, the request queue grew.
- Why it impacted Acme more: their traffic pattern uses high variability in prompt length and a higher rate of small bursts that triggered the heuristic more strongly on the shard set they were routed to.

Evidence attached: latency plots, batch-size distribution, and kv-cache trace file.

Proposed corrective actions (short-term <=72h):
- Revert the batching heuristic flag for affected clusters (done at 04:20 UTC — confirmed lower tail latency in canary).
- Tighten the per-tenant rollout policy and add feature-flagged kill-switch for long-running kernels (owner: Marcus).
- Add a guard that caps batch formation time for variable-length sequences (owner: Karthik).

Longer-term (>72h):
- Kernel-level timeout instrumentation and automated fallback to lower-concurrency kernels (owner: Grace + Infra).
- A workload profile gate that prevents heuristic from enabling for tenants with high prompt-length variance.

I’ll include the above in the RCA draft.

— Grace
Senior Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: acme_latency_plots.zip (zip)]
[Attachment: kv-cache-trace.txt (text)]

From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Sally Chen <sally.chen@acmetech.com>, Jordan Li <jordan.li@acmetech.com>
Cc: grace_oconnor@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, marcus_lin@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-04-04T14:05:00-07:00
Subject: [DRAFT] AcmeTech incident Apr 2 — RCA and corrective plan

Sally & Jordan — attaching our RCA draft and proposed corrective plan for your review. Key points up-front:
- Timeline: incident window Apr 2 22:10–22:45 UTC, automated mitigation (batch flag rollback) at 04:20 UTC on Apr 3 reduced errors.
- Root cause: rollout of a continuous-batching heuristic interacting with KV cache invalidation on a subset of shards; produced long-running GPU kernels and request queueing under bursty traffic.
- Impact: ~12% request failures for Acme during window; estimated 0.6% weekly revenue impact for Acme on that day.

Actions and owners (short-term):
- Marcus: feature-flag kill-switch + immediate rollout policy changes (ETA 48h).
- Karthik: implement batch formation cap and verify safe defaults (ETA 72h).
- Grace: kernel timeout instrumentation plan and post-deploy canary (ETA 2 weeks).
- Neha/Laura: customer communications, credit proposal, and exec readout scheduling (Neha to lead).

Credit & contractual ask: we propose a one-time service credit to Acme for the impact window while we fix the root cause. I will follow up with finance for approval and DocuSign if you accept.

Requested exec readout: Apr 5 14:00 UTC — 30 minutes. Please confirm who will attend from your side.

Attachment: acme_rca_draft.pdf (contains timeline, logs, mitigations, risk assessment).

Thanks for your patience. We’re treating this as top priority.

— Neha
Head of Customer Reliability, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: acme_rca_draft.pdf (pdf)]

Subject: Re: [DRAFT] AcmeTech incident Apr 2 — RCA and corrective plan

Neha — thank you for the quick triage and the draft. The technical analysis lines up with what we saw. Jordan and I can join the exec readout Apr 5 14:00 UTC. 

Credit: we accept the proposed one-time credit as a starting point; please share proposed amount and steps for DocuSign/finance. We will want a remediation commitment for the rollout policy and the guard for variable-length sequences.

One small ask for the readout: include an explicit rollback/playbook we can run from our side if we see similar symptoms again (so we can fail fast).

Sally

From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Sally Chen <sally.chen@acmetech.com>, Jordan Li <jordan.li@acmetech.com>
Cc: grace_oconnor@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, marcus_lin@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-04-05T15:28:00-07:00
Subject: Post-readout: decisions, commitments, and closure steps (AcmeTech)

Team — quick summary of what we agreed on during the readout and next steps for closure: 

1) Commitments accepted:
- One-time service credit to Acme: finance to propose amount by Apr 7; Neha/Laura to send DocuSign link once approved.
- Marcus to ship the feature-flag kill-switch and updated rollout policy by Apr 7 (owner: Marcus).
- Karthik to deliver batch formation cap + safe defaults by Apr 8 and run canary on 2 shards.
- Grace to produce kernel-timeout instrumentation PR and a 2-week plan for full rollout (target Apr 19).

2) Customer-run playbook: Laura will draft a simple fail-fast checklist (3 steps) Acme can run if they see symptoms; to be shared by EOD Apr 6.

3) Follow-up cadence: weekly check-ins for 4 weeks (owner: Neha). Final closure after 2 consecutive weeks of stable canary metrics.

4) Risks: we noted potential for other tenants with similar traffic patterns; infra will run a variance scan and flag other tenants for cautious rollout (Karthik, ETA Apr 9).

5) Attachments and links: RCA PDF, latency plots, kv-traces are in the shared Drive link (see related_links).

If anything above is incorrect or missing, reply-all with corrections. Otherwise I will move this thread to "monitoring" and track owners in our internal incident tracker.

Thanks everyone for a fast collaborative response.

— Neha
Neha Kapoor
Head of Customer Reliability, Redwood Inference
